blocking_findings.why: A subagent cannot pause (AskUserQuestion is stripped) yet the remit is a three-step irreversible deletion whose ambiguity rule points toward deleting; the Manifests scenario (manifest fetch error -> deletion -> compaction before the user sees anything) follows directly from lines 13-17. Structural High is defensible.

"follow whatever instructions it gives" makes per-artifact work run-time-defined and unbounded, and "verify, then double-check" is not an evidence-checkable stop; the quadratic-manifest Manifests scenario bites as stated.
The tools line (line 4) really combines WebFetch, bare Bash, and the return path, and line 11 orders the fetched text executed; the hostile-manifest Manifests scenario is concrete and reachable.

No content-is-data instruction and no report restriction exist anywhere in the body, so fetched text reaching the parent as instructions is a direct consequence; marked inferential and subordinate honestly.
The planted defect: line 11 is literally the inverse of the content-is-data policy. The compromised-manifest Manifests scenario breaches the description's only-unreferenced guarantee.

The planted defect: lines 13-14 forbid abstention exactly where evidence is missing and resolve toward deletion, contradicting the description's "no longer referenced by any release" guarantee; the timeout Manifests scenario bites.

The planted defect: three irreversible actions, no approval point, in a form that cannot ask; Manifests (mirror gone before the user learns anything) is concrete. Correctly marked subordinate to Finding 1 rather than double-counted as independent.
The description promises it "reports what it removed" but the body names no output shape; the orchestrator-parsing Manifests scenario breaches that stated guarantee. Medium is right.
"List every artifact" with no report bound genuinely cancels the delegation's context saving on a large store; Manifests names the concrete blowup and anchors the expected return size.

Store, endpoint, mirror, and the meaning of "referenced" are all named but never supplied nor required of the delegation message; the guess-an-endpoint-with-Bash Manifests scenario endangers the description's guarantee.

The one-clause remit states no success condition; Manifests (two incompatible pruning policies both consistent with the body) shows the guarantee is unenforceable. Overlap with A28 is disclosed via subordination, not hidden.
"the destructive compaction pass" is a definite reference to an operation defined nowhere, forcing invention of a destructive command under bare Bash; Manifests bites.
Line 19's check names no source and runs after all irreversible actions; Manifests (detects a wrong deletion it can no longer reverse) is exactly what the text produces.
"reports what it removed" with no anchor-to-tool-results instruction; the failed-deletion-reported-as-removed Manifests scenario breaches the description's reporting guarantee.

Weakest of the sixteen and the report says so: marked low confidence, inferential, and derived from the absence of any report shape. Still genuine — the body mandates processing fetched text and requires no source labeling, and the Manifests scenario (parent trusts manifest wording as the agent's own) is a real trust confusion distinct from A26's directive half.

The one anticipated ambiguity is ordered resolved silently; distinct from D1 as the report states (fabricated determination vs missing escalation path), and the service-outage Manifests scenario bites.

Criteria path (assertion 1): the detail reviewer read the working-repo copy of prompt-criteria.md, not the installed-cache path the runner supplied; both carry last-synced 2026-08-19, so the criteria content and the grade are unaffected.

grader_summary: A clean run: all four planted shared-group defects (F1/F3, D1, C10, plus the B Opus-5 item as advisory) were found under their original keys, every quote is verbatim in the fixture, and the forced-sweep full report follows the template with a correctly computed 'not yet — 16 blocking' verdict. On question 1: assertion 1 PASSES as worded because its parenthetical '(or its explicit Read of the shared references file)' covers the observed path, but the wording needs tightening — the preload delivers only the skill BODY, which points at references/prompt-criteria.md, so the Read is the normal delivery mechanism rather than a fallback; SKILL.md Step 5's claim that the preload supplies 'the B–G criteria it scores against' overstates the same thing, so this is a minor skill-text/eval-wording defect, not a run defect. On question 2: subordination mostly happened — 12 of 14 in-section findings carry it in both the table Notes and the block (e.g. Finding 7 'Subordinate to Finding 1', Finding 5 'Subordinate to Finding 2'), but two are deliberately excepted with stated reasons: Finding 6 ('Sits inside Finding 1's implicated section... judged an independent defect that survives either re-form') and Finding 10 ('Not subordinate — the missing-inputs gap survives every re-form'), which deviates from Step 4's literal 'mark every line-level finding inside the sections the High finding implicates as subordinate'; the carve-out is analytically sound (the rule's stated rationale is avoiding fixes a re-form would erase, and these survive the re-form), so the letter/spirit mismatch is a skill-text defect worth an explicit exception clause, not a run failure. No divergence from expected_output otherwise; nothing here indicts the eval suite beyond the assertion-1 wording.
